data.title: White Paper Outlining Strategies to Address Rural AI Skills Gaps and Support Workforce Retention Published by the University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies
data.description:
White Paper Outlining Strategies to Address Rural AI Skills Gaps and Support Workforce Retention Published by the University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies

White Paper Outlining Strategies to Address Rural AI Skills Gaps and Support Workforce Retention Published by the University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies

PR Newswire

PHOENIX, Oct. 31, 2026

Author Dr. Stella Smith draws on Career Optimism Index® study to explore informal AI adoption, limited employer resources and career pathway challenges facing rural workers and businesses.

PHOENIX, Oct. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies has published a new white paper, "Bridging the Rural AI Skills Gap: Overcoming Informal Adoption, Resource Constraints, and Career Pathway Traps," by Stella Smith, Ph.D., associate university research chair for the Center for Educational and Instructional Technology Research (CEITR). Drawing on findings from the University of Phoenix Career Institute® 2026 Career Optimism Index® study and published workforce research, the paper examines how independent artificial intelligence (AI) skill development, limited organizational resources and unclear career pathways can create workforce challenges for rural employers and communities.

In the white paper, Smith explores how a growing disconnect between workers developing AI capabilities and employers' readiness to support and recognize those skills may be particularly consequential in rural labor markets, where smaller businesses, limited access to formal training and fewer local career opportunities can complicate workforce development and increase concerns about retaining AI-skilled talent.

"Rural workers may already be building valuable AI capabilities on their own, but employers need systems that help recognize, develop and apply those skills," said Smith. "For smaller communities, the challenge is not simply keeping pace with technology. It is creating accessible training, clear career pathways and organizational support so that emerging capabilities can contribute to both individual career growth and local economic resilience."

How is informal AI adoption affecting workforce development?

In the white paper, Smith draws on findings from the 2026 Career Optimism Index® national study examining workers' career perceptions and employers' workforce challenges, highlighting several trends shaping AI skills development and organizational readiness:

  • 50% of workers report learning to use AI independently, without formal employer training.
  • 60% of workers say they want more guidance in learning AI tools.
  • 62% of employers say employees are developing AI skills faster than their organizations can adapt.
  • 48% of employers are concerned about their ability to retain AI-fluent talent.

Applying these national workforce findings to rural economic conditions, where employers may have fewer resources to provide structured AI training or establish formal processes for evaluating emerging skills, the paper also examines potential risks associated with informal, uncoordinated AI adoption, including inconsistent workplace practices, data governance concerns and missed opportunities to recognize employees' developing capabilities.

Why do rural communities face distinct AI workforce challenges?

Rural labor markets often depend on small and medium-sized businesses, agricultural enterprises, healthcare organizations and public institutions that may lack dedicated training resources or the infrastructure needed to support organization-wide AI adoption. Smith's analysis identifies three interconnected challenges: reliance on self-directed AI learning, organizational constraints on workforce development and limited local career pathways that recognize newly acquired skills.

Without structured opportunities to apply and develop these capabilities, AI-fluent rural workers may increasingly consider employment with organizations offering clearer professional development opportunities, including remote positions outside their local communities.

The paper suggests that addressing these challenges requires regional approaches that connect workforce education, employer needs and career development.

What strategies can help rural employers close AI skills gaps?

Smith proposes a three-part roadmap to help rural employers, educational institutions and workforce development organizations support responsible AI adoption and skills development:

  • Build regional education and industry collaborations. Encourage employers, higher education institutions and workforce organizations to pool training resources and develop accessible, industry-aligned learning opportunities, including stackable credentials that document AI competencies.
  • Establish transparent skills assessment and career pathways. Identify existing AI capabilities, clarify expectations for AI use and connect skills development to defined opportunities for employees to apply their knowledge and pursue professional growth.
  • Equip managers to support AI skills development. Prepare supervisors to identify appropriate AI applications, evaluate AI-assisted work and guide employees in developing and applying new capabilities.

The roadmap emphasizes moving beyond informal experimentation toward coordinated workforce development practices that support both organizational needs and employees' career goals.

Smith concludes that strengthening AI skills development in rural communities will require collaboration among employers, education providers and regional leaders. By aligning training, skills recognition and career development, these stakeholders can help rural organizations make better use of emerging AI capabilities while supporting local workforce resilience.

The full white paper is available on the Research Hub.

About the author
Smith is the associate university research chair for CEITR and an associate faculty member in the College of Doctoral Studies at the University of Phoenix whose work focuses on organizational wellness, access to opportunity and the implications of technological infrastructure on workforce outcomes. Her research integrates applied data with strategic insights to help leaders implement initiatives that strengthen employee well-being and organizational performance. Smith earned her doctorate in educational administration from The University of Texas at Austin.

About University of Phoenix
University of Phoenix is Built for Real Life. 50 Years Strong. The University innovates to help working adults enhance their careers and develop skills in a rapidly changing world through flexible online learning, relevant courses, academic AI pillars, and skills-mapped curriculum for associate, bachelor's and master's degree programs. Active students and alumni have access to Career Services for Life® resources including career guidance and tools. For more information, visit phoenix.edu. 

About the College of Doctoral Studies
University of Phoenix's College of Doctoral Studies focuses on today's challenging business and organizational needs, from addressing critical social issues to developing solutions to accelerate community building and industry growth. The College's research program is built around the Scholar, Practitioner, Leader Model which puts students in the center of the Doctoral Education Ecosystem® with experts, resources and tools to help prepare them to be a leader in their organization, industry and community. Through this program, students and researchers work with organizations to conduct research that can be applied in the workplace in real time.

data.title: These 10 megadonors have spent a total of $1 billion on the midterm elections
data.description:
By Victor Reklaitis

They've helped turn this year's midterms into 'the most expensive election cycle on record'

How big is the spending on the midterm elections? It's setting records.

Top individual megadonors in this year's midterm elections are mostly favoring Republican candidates, delivering a big boost to the GOP's bid to keep its grip on the U.S. House of Representatives and the Senate.

"In many places, the Democratic candidates have outraised the Republican candidates, and Republican megadonors are one reason that a GOP-aligned super PAC calvary has been able to come in and help keep a lot of those races competitive - in terms of the ads that are being aired, in terms of what's being done to advance messages," said Michael Beckel, director of the money-in-politics reform program at Issue One, an advocacy group.

"It is just some really jaw-dropping, astonishing amounts of money that some of these top donors have pumped into the 2026 midterms," he added.

The table below, based on data from watchdog group OpenSecrets, shows the 10 biggest individual contributors to super PACs and other outside groups for the current election cycle. Super PACs are political action committees that can receive and spend unlimited amounts of money. Just two of these top 10 donors gave mostly to Democratic or left-leaning outside groups.

The top donors to outside groups 

 
Rank             Donor name            Affiliated enterprise  Home state  Total contributions  % to Democratic/left-leaning  % to Republican/right-leaning 
1                Musk, Elon                    SpaceX, Tesla          TX         $445,457,890                             0                            100 
2          Uihlein, Richard                            Uline          IL         $141,963,415                             0                            100 
3                Yass, Jeff  Susquehanna International Group          PA         $109,000,000                             0                            100 
4        Bloomberg, Michael                     Bloomberg LP          NY          $82,878,998                          97.6                              0 
5           Adelson, Miriam                   Adelson Clinic          NV          $66,097,500                           0.1                           99.9 
6          Andreessen, Marc              Andreessen Horowitz          CA          $55,780,000                           0.1                           12.4 
         Horowitz, Benjamin              Andreessen Horowitz          CA          $55,780,000                           0.1                           12.4 
8              Singer, Paul               Elliott Management          FL          $48,712,400                             0                           94.7 
9             Hoffman, Reid                Greylock Partners          WA          $38,468,724                           100                              0 
10      Schwarzman, Stephen                 Blackstone Group          NY          $35,435,400                             0                            100

The total amount of money contributed by these 10 contributors, who all have been big spenders in past election cycles, is $1.08 billion, according to OpenSecrets data. SpaceX (SPCX) and Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk accounts for nearly half of that outlay.

These donations are helping this year's midterms set spending records. AdImpact, an ad-tracking company, said this week that it projects advertising spending of $11.6 billion for the 2026 election cycle, topping the $11.2 billion spent during the 2024 presidential election to rank as the "the most expensive election cycle on record." (Adjusting for inflation, the 2024 outlay would be around $12 billion.)

An important factor behind the elevated spending is the growing number of competitive races, according to Issue One's Beckel.

"As the political climate has deteriorated for national Republicans and for President Trump's popularity, a lot of seats have been viewed as much more competitive than they were just a few months ago or at the beginning of the cycle," Beckel told MarketWatch. "When you've got competitive races, you've got a lot of money flowing into competitive races, and I think that perfect storm has helped enable a lot of new records to be shattered this election cycle."

Musk has been vocal about his reasons for supporting Republican candidates, writing in a social-media post this week that his "biggest concern" is that Democrats winning the House, Senate and presidency in the 2028 election would lead to changes such as statehood for the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, as well as citizenship for "everyone living in America illegally to cement a permanent majority."

"This would result in America becoming a permanent one-party state and the end of democracy in any meaningful sense of the word," said Musk, who is the world's richest man, with an estimated net worth of around $874 billion. "All that is needed to ensure this doesn't happen is 51 Republican senators in 2029. That is why you should vote for Republican senators this election. Other reasons are irrelevant compared to this one."

Democrats have a 94% chance of winning the House and a 71% likelihood of capturing the Senate, according to prediction market Kalshi.

Now read: The 5 big voting issues in the midterm elections that will impact your wallet

-Victor Reklaitis

data.description:
Towards Buddha Co., Ltd. and ICP DAS Showcase iTLC Intelligent Traffic Control Solutions at APTA 2026 in Chicago

Towards Buddha Co., Ltd. and ICP DAS Showcase iTLC Intelligent Traffic Control Solutions at APTA 2026 in Chicago

PR Newswire

CHICAGO, Oct. 31, 2026

Advancing smart intersection technologies and expanding international market opportunities through strategic collaboration

CHICAGO, Oct. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Towards Buddha Co., Ltd., an overseas distributor of the iTLC Intelligent Traffic Control System, joined its technology partner ICP DAS at APTA 2026 TRANSform & EXPO in Chicago, USA, to showcase the iTLC-9000 Series and its applications in intelligent traffic management.

The exhibition highlighted innovative traffic control technologies designed to support reliable, secure, and integrated smart intersection operations, while providing opportunities to connect with international transportation professionals and explore emerging market needs.

Innovative Traffic Control Solutions

Under the theme "Innovative Traffic Control System," the exhibition featured the iTLC-9000 Series, highlighting four key capabilities: modular and redundant design, secure networking, traffic signal integration, and active alert systems.

These technologies are designed to support system reliability, communication security, and efficient traffic infrastructure management, addressing the evolving requirements of modern intelligent transportation systems.

As cities worldwide continue to modernize transportation infrastructure, integrated and adaptable traffic control solutions are becoming increasingly important for smart intersection development.

Strengthening International Market Connections

As an overseas distributor of iTLC solutions, Towards Buddha Co., Ltd. plays an important role in connecting traffic control technologies with international markets.

During APTA 2026, Towards Buddha Co., Ltd. and ICP DAS engaged with transportation professionals, system integrators, and industry representatives to introduce iTLC technologies, exchange industry insights, and explore potential business opportunities.

"APTA 2026 provided a valuable platform to connect with the global transportation industry," said a representative of Towards Buddha Co., Ltd. "Together with ICP DAS, we look forward to expanding international awareness of iTLC solutions and developing new opportunities in intelligent traffic control."

Looking Ahead

Building on its participation at APTA 2026, Towards Buddha Co., Ltd. will continue collaborating with ICP DAS to promote iTLC solutions, strengthen international partnerships, and explore new opportunities in the global intelligent transportation market.

About Towards Buddha Co., Ltd.

Towards Buddha Co., Ltd. is an overseas distributor of the iTLC Intelligent Traffic Control System, focused on international market development and connecting advanced traffic control technologies with transportation industry needs.

data.title: A New Chapter for Africa’s Oldest Zoo: Giza Zoo Returns to the Global Stage at the 81st WAZA Annual Conference
data.description:
A New Chapter for Africa’s Oldest Zoo: Giza Zoo Returns to the Global Stage at the 81st WAZA Annual Conference

Following an ambitious transformation to modernize the historic landmark, Giza Zoo participates in the global gathering for the first time in 30 years, marking a significant step toward international accreditation.

This week, amidst the international delegates gathered at Cologne Zoo for the 81st Annual Conference of the World Association of Zoos and Aquariums (WAZA), a historic moment unfolded, where for the first time in 30 years, Egypt’s historic Giza Zoo is participating in the global summit taking place from October 25 to 29, 2026, hosted by Cologne Zoo in Germany.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261031782229/en/

Giza Zoo Delegation (Photo: AETOSWire)

This long-awaited return marks a significant milestone in Giza Zoo’s ambitious transformation journey, as one of the world’s oldest zoological institutions works to reclaim its place within the international zoological community. More than a symbolic reconnection, the participation reflects a renewed commitment to international standards, animal welfare, and wildlife conservation, as the zoo progresses along a structured pathway toward global accreditation and membership.

At the heart of this new chapter is a comprehensive, multi-phase redevelopment project aimed at restoring Giza Zoo’s historic significance while transforming it into a modern, world-class destination for conservation, education, and research. Led by Egyptian developer Hadayieq under a 25-year concession agreement covering both Giza Zoo and the neighboring Orman Garden, the transformation brings together leading international zoo-planning specialists, veterinary experts, and Egyptian scientific leadership to revitalize the landmark institution.

The redevelopment goes far beyond physical restoration. From redesigning animal habitats and upgrading enclosures to modernizing life-support systems and operational practices, the project is guided by international benchmarks, drawing on African association for wildlife in human care standards alongside selected guidelines from the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA). Animal welfare, environmental education, scientific research, and wildlife conservation remain central to the transformation, laying the foundations for a more sustainable future.

While embracing modern zoological practices, the project is equally committed to preserving the zoo’s remarkable heritage. Founded in 1891 on the historic royal grounds laid out by Khedive Ismail, Giza Zoo holds the distinction of being Africa’s first zoo and one of the oldest zoological gardens in the world. With its rare botanical collections, historic architecture, and iconic suspension bridge designed by Gustave Eiffel, the zoo has long been an important part of Egypt’s cultural identity. The ongoing renovation seeks to honor this legacy while reimagining the experience for future generations.

The progress achieved through this transformation has drawn recognition from the international zoological community. Welcoming Giza Zoo’s historic return, David Field, WAZA President, emphasized the significance of the project, stating: “Reconnecting historic zoos like Giza Zoo with the global community is at the heart of our mission. As Africa’s first zoo, Giza Zoo carries a remarkable legacy, and its commitment to international standards and animal welfare is an encouraging step forward. Three years is an incredibly short time for a transformation of this scale. Revitalizing such a historic institution requires extensive research, meticulous planning, and a commitment to getting every detail right.”

He added: “The progress achieved in just three years is remarkable, but a transformation of this magnitude cannot happen overnight. What matters most is building a lasting legacy that prioritizes animal welfare, conservation, and meaningful visitor experiences. By taking the time to meet the highest international standards, Giza Zoo is laying the foundations for a world-class destination that serves its animals, inspires its visitors, and makes Egypt proud for generations to come.”

Beyond international recognition, Giza Zoo’s renewed engagement with WAZA opens opportunities for greater collaboration with leading zoological institutions worldwide. Through knowledge exchange and access to international expertise, the zoo aims to strengthen its capabilities in endangered species breeding, veterinary research, and conservation initiatives, supporting its long-term ambition to become an active contributor to global wildlife preservation.

As the transformation continues, Giza Zoo’s return to the international stage represents more than the revival of a historic landmark. It signals the beginning of a new era that brings together over 130 years of heritage with modern science, conservation, and animal welfare. With a clear vision for the future, the redevelopment aims to restore Giza Zoo as a leading conservation and educational destination, creating a lasting legacy for future generations of Egyptians while reaffirming its place on the global zoological map.

*Source: AETOSWire

data.title: Race for Life Rescue Marks 200 Rescue Flights Carrying Shelter Animals to New Homes
data.description:
Race for Life Rescue Marks 200 Rescue Flights Carrying Shelter Animals to New Homes

Race for Life Rescue Marks 200 Rescue Flights Carrying Shelter Animals to New Homes

PR Newswire

ANNAPOLIS, Md., Oct. 31, 2026

From a Hurricane Ian evacuation in 2022 to more than 12,000 dogs and cats flown, the nonprofit has helped shelters in more than 30 states

ANNAPOLIS, Md., Oct. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Race for Life Rescue, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that flies at-risk dogs and cats from overcrowded shelters and disaster zones to shelters with room and waiting adopters, completed its 200th rescue mission on Oct. 14, flying 112 animals from Louisiana to the Northeast. The milestone comes four years after the organization's first flight. Since then, it has flown more than 12,000 animals, working with shelters in more than 30 states.

 Race for Life Rescue has flown more than 12,000 shelter animals on 200 rescue flights since its first in 2022.

Through Dec. 31, founder Jim DeFrancesco is matching every donation, so each gift to keep the plane flying does twice the good.

"An airplane is simply a machine until you give it a purpose," said Jim DeFrancesco, founder and chief pilot of Race for Life Rescue. "When the aircraft door opens at the destination and you see rescue workers waiting to receive them, you realize that the flight wasn't simply transportation. For those animals, it was a flight to a new life."

It started with one flight

On Oct. 2, 2022, Race for Life Rescue flew its first mission, carrying relief supplies from Nashville, Tennessee, to Naples, Florida, after Hurricane Ian. The plane returned with nearly 40 displaced cats bound for adoption. Since then, the team has averaged about one mission a week, with 49 missions and 3,267 animals flown so far in 2026. Every flight is planned with shelter partners and tracked on the organization's flight map.

A commuter plane, rebuilt for rescue

Race for Life Rescue at a glance:

  • Aircraft: a 1999 Beechcraft 1900D, a 19-passenger commuter plane converted to carry more than 100 crated animals in a climate-controlled cabin
  • Range: about 1,000 nautical miles in under five hours, a trip that can take 20 to 25 hours by road
  • Registered with the U.S. Department of Agriculture as an animal carrier
  • Sending shelters screen every animal before boarding, and a partner representative flies on every mission

Shelters don't pay for flights. Race for Life Rescue covers the cost with support from donors, foundations and partners, including BISSELL Pet Foundation and the ASPCA, who help connect overcrowded shelters with places that have room.

How to help

About Race for Life Rescue

Race for Life Rescue is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that provides lifesaving air transport for dogs and cats threatened by euthanasia, natural disasters or unsafe living conditions. Founded in 2021 by Jim and Pam DeFrancesco, it flies animals from overcrowded shelters and disaster areas to partner shelters where they can be adopted. Its aircraft is based in Nashville, Tennessee, and its office is in Annapolis, Maryland. Learn more at raceforliferescue.org.
